transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2025-12-11
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Recording: Fireflies auto transcript

Summary / topics (auto): integration patterns, SDKs, LangChain, gateway proxy, quotas, observability, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs

00:00 Maya Chen: All right mm thanks everyone for joining, I think we can get started. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Luis is our solutions engineer.
00:08 Priya Kapoor: Hi, Priya here, thanks, we have Tom and Sara also from infra. Kenji might join a bit late.
00:14 Luis Ortega: Hey, everyone. Quick agenda — 1) understand your stack and goals, 2) integration patterns (SDKs / LangChain / gateway), 3) infra constraints (VPC, allowlist, quotas), 4) next steps for a POC. Sound good?
00:23 Tom Erickson: Yep that's perfect.

00:36 Maya Chen: Priya, can you give us a quick picture of what you're trying to build and what success looks like?
00:42 Priya Kapoor: Sure, so Cygnus ML is building an internal agent layer for our analytics product. We want to add a natural language assistant for customers and also power some internal automation. Success is sub-100ms token latency p95 for interactive flows, and cost under a threshold for 1M tokens / month — but we are flexible if latency requirements push us toward Dedicated. We also have strict data residency for EU customers.
01:05 Sara Nguyen: From infra, we need SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. For production we'd prefer VPC or a private deployment that can sit in our account, but we might start with Hosted if the security docs line up.
01:17 Maya Chen: Great — that's consistent with other customers. Quick question on your dev stack: are you using LangChain or LlamaIndex as part of the orchestrator?
01:26 Priya Kapoor: Kenji has been prototyping with LangChain for the orchestration and LlamaIndex for retrieval — mostly on top of open models. We want to keep the code using the usual LangChain abstractions.
01:36 Luis Ortega: Perfect, we have SDKs and adapters that fit LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns — small code drops, sometimes a wrapper at the gateway layer. For example, we provide a LangChain LLM wrapper and an embeddings endpoint that maps well to LlamaIndex's retriever.
01:52 Tom Erickson: We currently run Kong as our API gateway, and we're exploring putting a proxy in front of Redwood so that we can centralize auth and rate limits — is that a supported pattern?
02:03 Luis Ortega: Absolutely. Common setup: Kong or Envoy in front, mTLS between gateway and Redwood, token exchange or signed requests. You can use our API key model or a short-lived token from your identity provider; both patterns exist. Note — if you want per-customer quotas and fine-grained rate limits, we recommend doing that at the gateway and also configuring Redwood rate limits to protect the runtime.
02:25 Sara Nguyen: How does rate limiting on Redwood side work? We need hierarchical quotas — org, team, and route-based limits.
02:33 Luis Ortega: We support per-key quotas, per-route limits, and token-based throttling. There's also a bursts config for Dedicated where you can allow temporary burst above commit. We'll share the bloom — I mean the burst policy doc — with exact fields.
02:48 Priya Kapoor: (laughs) the bloom, burst — nice.

03:01 Maya Chen: For orchestration, typical choices we've seen: 1) direct SDK calls from service -> Redwood hosted API, 2) service -> internal gateway -> Redwood (recommended for orgs wanting central auth & observability), 3) private deployment with internal network for strict compliance. Any preference?
03:18 Tom Erickson: We like gateway option 2 for initial rollout. It fits our observability pipelines and lets us keep logs centralized. For stricter data requirements we'd move to private later.
03:27 Luis Ortega: Makes sense. With gateway you'll want to run a short-circuit cache for repeated prompts — Redwood supports prefix/KV caching which plays well with a proxy layer.
03:39 Sara Nguyen: Observability — can we get token-level breakdowns and traces? We need to connect to Datadog and an internal tracing system.
03:48 Luis Ortega: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-request latency, token breakdowns and trace IDs. You can forward traces via OpenTelemetry and export logs to your SIEM. We'll include a short doc on hooking up Datadog and an example OTLP config.
04:04 Priya Kapoor: On the embeddings side we need deterministic embeddings for LlamaIndex. Are there any quirks with the hosted models?
04:13 Luis Ortega: Determinism depends on model selection and temperature. For embeddings, they are deterministic by design (for the same model), but quantization or slight version differences can matter. We recommend pinning a model revision for the POC — that's easy in both Hosted and Dedicated.
04:28 Kenji Ito: (joins) Sorry late — quick q: If we use LangChain, is it a major refactor to swap between Hosted and Dedicated?
04:36 Luis Ortega: Not at all — our SDKs abstract the endpoint and config. You'd change the base_url and maybe the auth flow. For LangChain we have a small adapter patch — two to three lines to swap endpoints. We'll send the snippet.
04:50 Tom Erickson: For the POC, what kind of benchmark should we run to validate latency?
04:55 Maya Chen: Good question. We usually ask for your typical prompt set (we recommend 100 prompts representing different user journeys) and a concurrency profile. For Dedicated we can simulate p95 under target QPS and show tail-latency with/without caching. We'll run an internal mini-benchmark and share results.
05:12 Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Cost: do you have guidelines for cost per 1k tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted?
05:19 Maya Chen: We'll send the pricing sheet; Hosted is simpler but Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale and predictable latency. There's also our Optimize recommendations — batching and quantization tips to lower cost without breaking latency SLOs.
05:33 Sara Nguyen: Network / compliance question: for Private/VPC, can Redwood deploy in our AWS account or do you require cross-account access?
05:41 Luis Ortega: We offer a customer-managed VPC option where the runtime sits in your account with a control plane that can be private. For air-gapped/on-prem there's an on-prem package too. We'll attach the network diagram and list of required endpoints and IPs.
05:56 Tom Erickson: Good. Any gotchas with KV cache and LlamaIndex? We use chunked docs and retrieval.
06:04 Luis Ortega: KV cache is per-session/prefix; for retrieval flows it's often fine — you'll want to control cache TTLs, invalidation on document updates, and ensure embedding vector refresh pipelines. We'll include recommended TTL values for typical retrieval patterns.
06:18 Priya Kapoor: For the gateway auth, we want SAML/SSO integration for access to the Console only — can Redwood do SSO for multiple tenant roles?
06:27 Maya Chen: Yes, Console supports SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC for roles. For programmatic access we use API keys or short-lived tokens and can tie those back to users via the identity provider.

06:40 Maya Chen: Let's surface a few risks or blockers early — any strict procurement or legal windows?
06:45 Priya Kapoor: Procurement timeline is Q1 budget cycle — ideally POC results before end of year so the team can push a budget ask. Legal will want SOC2, Data Processing Agreement, and IP/usage terms.
06:56 Maya Chen: Understood. We'll send SOC2 summary and the DPA template.
07:02 Tom Erickson: For request routing: if capacity is constrained in one region, can Redwood failover to another region or to a cheaper model automatically?
07:12 Luis Ortega: Yes, smart routing can fallback to model variants or other regions based on policy. For strict residency you'd lock to region; for flexibility you can set cost vs latency policies. We'll show examples in the rollout docs.
07:28 Kenji Ito: One more thing — debug traces: if a user reports a weird response, can we replay the request fully including tokens and KV state?
07:36 Luis Ortega: You can capture full request traces and we provide replay tooling for POC and debugging; for security you can mask PII before storing traces. That is a common ask from customers.
07:50 Priya Kapoor: Great — are there example projects or quickstarts?
07:54 Luis Ortega: Yes, we have a LangChain quickstart repo, LlamaIndex notebook, and a sample gateway proxy pattern example. I'll drop links.
08:02 Maya Chen: Ok let's do a quick recap and align on next steps.
08:06 Maya Chen: Action items — Maya will share pricing and SOC2 summary; Luis will share LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets, gateway proxy pattern, and a small benchmark script; Priya/Sara will share prompts, throughput and network allowlist. Aim to kick off a week-long POC in the week of 2025-12-22.
08:23 Priya Kapoor: That works for us. Thanks everyone.
08:28 Tom Erickson: Thanks.
08:31 Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and proposed POC plan.
08:35 (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and filler. References shared: deck link (https://redwood.ai/decks/integration-proxy-patterns), LangChain quickstart (https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-quickstart), SOC2 summary (link shared on email).
